en.commentary:
I rank a nootropic on one question: can I read the label and find a clinically studied ingredient at a clinically studied dose? Mind Lab Pro v4 answers that eleven times on a single panel, which is why it takes first place at $69 for a thirty-day supply. Cognizin citicoline at 250 mg, bacopa standardized to 24 percent bacosides, lion's mane fruiting body and Suntheanine L-theanine all appear in plain milligrams, and the whole formula runs caffeine free so I keep control of my own stimulant load with my morning coffee.

Performance Lab Mind lands second because it does the same job with four ingredients at $59, which makes it the cleanest base layer for anyone already taking creatine, omega-3 or their own caffeine.

Third place goes to Jarrow Citicoline at $33.99 for 120 capsules. Citicoline carries the deepest human trial record of any single compound in this category, and at roughly 28 cents a day this is where I send anyone who wants the evidence on its own. Qualia Mind delivers the widest ingredient panel here and I feel it on heavy writing days, with $139 a bottle placing it in a different budget conversation. Thorne Memoractiv earns its position on manufacturing standards, since Thorne runs four third-party certifications and supplies NSF Certified for Sport lines to professional teams.

The 2026 market backs this framing. Nootropics now sit in a category worth roughly $6 to $7 billion and growing at a double-digit annual rate, and more than 61 percent of buyers say they want plant-based, naturally sourced formulas. That demand is exactly what pushed transparent, fully dosed labels to the front of the shelf.

My practical advice: pick one product, run it for eight weeks, and hold the rest of your routine steady. Bacopa and lion's mane need that long to show anything measurable. Citicoline and L-theanine work inside an hour, so start there if you want a same-day read on whether this category does anything for you.

highlights.title: Mind Lab Pro v4 is the bottle I would buy first, and the label is the reason
highlights.body: Eleven nootropics, every one printed with its own milligram figure, is the rarest thing in this category. Cognizin citicoline at 250 mg matches the dose used in published attention work, the bacopa is standardized to 24 percent bacosides rather than sold as raw herb weight, and the lion's mane is fruiting body. At $69 for thirty servings it costs $2.30 a day, and the caffeine-free build means I can drink my usual coffee and still know exactly how much stimulant I took.

highlights.title: Citicoline alone at 28 cents a day is the smartest entry point in this whole category
highlights.body: Jarrow sells 120 capsules of 250 mg citicoline for $33.99, and citicoline is the compound in this space with the deepest human trial record behind attention and processing speed. Anyone new to nootropics should run this single ingredient for a month before spending $139 on a twenty-compound stack. It gives you a clean read on whether your brain responds to choline support, and that answer tells you which of the bigger formulas is worth your money.

highlights.title: Caffeine-free formulas win because they let you control the stimulant separately
highlights.body: Mind Lab Pro, Performance Lab Mind, NooCube and Thorne Memoractiv all leave caffeine out, and I score that as a design advantage. Your caffeine tolerance shifts week to week and your coffee habit already sets a baseline. Keeping the stimulant in your cup and the cognitive support in your capsule means you can adjust one without disturbing the other, and it keeps an afternoon dose available when you need focus late in the day.

highlights.title: Eight weeks is the honest trial period for anything herbal
highlights.body: Bacopa monnieri trials that show memory improvement run twelve weeks, and lion's mane work runs eight to sixteen. If you judge a bacopa-based formula after five days you are measuring your sleep quality, not the supplement. Buy a two-month supply, keep your sleep and training steady while you take it, and write down one concrete measure such as how far into an afternoon you can hold deep work. That is the only way to get a signal out of the noise.

highlights.title: Published certificates of analysis separate the top of this list from the rest
highlights.body: Thorne carries four third-party certifications and manufactures NSF Certified for Sport lines for professional teams. Nootropics Depot publishes certificates of analysis by lot number, so you can look up the exact bottle in your hand. In a supplement category where potency claims are easy to print and hard to check, that level of documentation is worth paying for, and it is a large part of why both brands rank where they do.

zh-tw.commentary:
老實說，益智補給這種東西我只看一件事：標示上有沒有寫清楚成分和劑量，而且那個劑量背後有沒有人體研究撐著。

Mind Lab Pro v4 排第一，就是因為它把這件事做了十一次。Cognizin citicoline 250 毫克、標準化到 24% bacosides 的假馬齒莧、猴頭菇子實體、Suntheanine 茶胺酸，全部用毫克老老實實印在瓶身上。而且整罐不含咖啡因，我可以照常喝我的早餐店冰美式，咖啡因要抓多少自己說了算。一個月份 69 美金，換算一天七十幾塊台幣，跟你每天那杯手搖差不多的價位。

Performance Lab Mind 排第二，四個成分、59 美金，如果你本來就在吃肌酸、魚油，或是自己補咖啡因，這罐是最乾淨的底層。

第三名 Jarrow Citicoline 我認為是整份榜單裡最划算的一罐。120 顆 33.99 美金，一天不到十塊台幣，而 citicoline 是這個品類裡人體試驗資料最厚的單一成分。想先確認自己對這類東西有沒有反應的人，我一律建議從這罐開始。

Qualia Mind 的成分表最豐富，趕稿那幾天我確實感覺得出來，只是一瓶 139 美金，那已經是另一個預算層級的討論了。Thorne Memoractiv 則是贏在製造標準，Thorne 手上四張第三方認證，NSF Certified for Sport 那條產線是直接供職業運動隊的。

市場面也支持這個判斷。益智補給 2026 年的規模大概落在 60 到 70 億美金，年成長率維持在兩位數，而且超過 61% 的消費者明講他們要植物來源的天然配方。這股需求就是把「劑量標示清楚」的產品推到貨架最前面的原因。

給你一個很實際的建議：一次只吃一罐，連續吃滿八週，其他作息盡量維持不變。假馬齒莧和猴頭菇本來就要八週才看得出東西。citicoline 和茶胺酸一小時內就有感，想當天就知道有沒有用，從這兩個下手最快。

en.commentary:
Mind Lab Pro v4 holds first on transparency, which is the only thing that lets you evaluate a nootropic before you take it. Every ingredient is listed at its exact dose with no proprietary blend hiding the amounts, and the doses match what the underlying studies used. A blend that lists eleven ingredients and one total milligram figure is telling you nothing, and most of this category does exactly that.

Citicoline at third deserves specific attention. Jarrow's CDP-Choline 250 is a single ingredient at a studied dose, and citicoline has among the better evidence bases here for attention and processing speed. If you want to know whether a nootropic works for you, start with one compound rather than a stack of eleven, because a stack that works gives you no information about which part did the work.

Lion's mane at sixth is worth noting given a September 2025 systematic review supporting it for cognitive function and for anxiety and depression markers. That is stronger evidence than most ingredients in this category carry.

Prevagen sits last, and I want to state plainly why. Its active ingredient is a protein that digestion breaks down before absorption, and its marketing claims have drawn regulatory and legal challenge. There are better places to put your money, and nine of them are listed above it.

highlights.title: Proprietary blends exist so you cannot evaluate the dose
highlights.body: A label listing eleven ingredients under one total milligram figure tells you nothing about whether any of them is present at a studied amount. Mind Lab Pro v4 lists every ingredient at its exact dose, matched to the studies behind it. If a brand will not disclose per-ingredient amounts, treat that as a decision they made about what you should be able to verify.

highlights.title: Start with one compound if you want to learn anything
highlights.body: Jarrow's Citicoline CDP-Choline 250 is a single ingredient at a studied dose, and citicoline carries among the better evidence bases here for attention and processing speed. An eleven-ingredient stack that works tells you nothing about which component did it, and stacks that do nothing leave you with no next step. Single ingredients produce information you can act on.

highlights.title: Lion's mane has the strongest recent evidence in this category
highlights.body: A September 2025 systematic review supported lion's mane for cognitive function alongside anxiety and depression markers, which is a stronger evidence base than most ingredients here carry. Nootropics Depot's 8:1 dual extract specifies both the extraction ratio and the method, which matters because water-only extracts miss the compounds a dual extraction captures.

highlights.title: Prevagen ranks last for a specific reason
highlights.body: Its active ingredient is a protein, and digestion breaks proteins down into amino acids before absorption, so the mechanism its marketing describes is difficult to reconcile with how digestion works. Its advertising claims have also faced regulatory and legal challenge. Nine products above it in this ranking give you better-evidenced ingredients at comparable or lower prices.

en.commentary:
The 2026 evidence rankings have settled around six ingredients with real human clinical data: bacopa monnieri, citicoline, lion's mane, L-theanine, rhodiola rosea and vitamin B12. That list is short, and it is the most useful filter available for a category where most products are built around ingredients with rodent studies and a good story.

Jarrow Citicoline moves to 9.0 overall with evidence at 9.6, the highest score on this board. Citicoline is a direct precursor to acetylcholine, the neurotransmitter most tied to attention and memory formation, and human trials support improved attention and focus particularly in older adults and people with mild cognitive decline. It is also among the best-tolerated compounds in the nootropic literature. At its price, buying a single well-dosed ingredient with this evidence base is the most rational purchase in the category, and value at 9.8 reflects that.

Mind Lab Pro v4 keeps first place on transparency at 9.8. Every ingredient is disclosed at its exact dose with no proprietary blend hiding behind a total milligram figure. In a category this loosely regulated, knowing what you are taking is the precondition for everything else.

I raised Nootropics Depot Lion's Mane to 8.4. Lion's mane has a mechanism nothing else here shares, which is stimulation of nerve growth factor and BDNF. That is a structural, slow-acting pathway rather than an acute one, so it belongs in a stack you evaluate over eight weeks.

One caution on stacking: citicoline, lion's mane and phosphatidylserine work through complementary pathways and combine coherently. Adding a fourth stimulant on top of that is where people start reporting jitteriness and disrupted sleep.

highlights.title: Six ingredients have real human data
highlights.body: Bacopa monnieri, citicoline, lion's mane, L-theanine, rhodiola rosea and vitamin B12 are where the 2026 clinical evidence rankings landed. Use that list as your filter. Most products in this category are built around compounds with rodent studies and a persuasive origin story, and separating the two is most of the work of buying well.

highlights.title: Citicoline is the most rational purchase here
highlights.body: It is a direct acetylcholine precursor with human trials supporting attention and memory, and it is among the best-tolerated compounds in the literature. Jarrow delivers it as a single well-dosed ingredient at a price that earns 9.8 on value, and evidence goes to 9.6, the top score on this board.

en.commentary: Mind Lab Pro v4 holds first at 9.3 and I want to be transparent about what I am scoring, because this category contains the widest gap between marketing and evidence of anything I cover. I score ingredient transparency, dose adequacy against published trials, and whether the specific compounds have human data rather than mechanistic speculation. Mind Lab Pro publishes every ingredient with its exact amount, uses no proprietary blend, and doses citicoline, bacopa, and lion's mane at levels that match the studies rather than at a fraction that fits a cost target. That is the whole basis of the ranking. Performance Lab Mind and Jarrow Citicoline 250 share 9.0 for a related reason, which is simplicity. Citicoline has the most consistent human evidence of any ingredient in this category for attention and processing speed, and a single-ingredient citicoline product at an effective dose delivers the best-supported effect at the lowest cost. If you want to try one thing in this category, that is the honest starting point. I have Prevagen at 5.9 at the bottom of this board and I want to state plainly why: its active ingredient is a jellyfish protein, and proteins are digested into amino acids in the stomach, so the mechanism the marketing describes does not survive contact with basic physiology. My practical advice: sleep, exercise, and caffeine timing produce larger cognitive effects than anything on this list. Fix those first, then experiment. No rank or score changes today.

en.commentary:
The useful development this week is a round-up of what the three existing human trials on lion's mane actually found, and it is worth reading before you spend money on the category's most hyped mushroom. The strongest of the three is the 2009 randomised controlled trial in adults with mild cognitive impairment, dosed at 750 mg three times daily, which showed a significant improvement in cognitive scores against placebo. Note that dose. It is 2,250 mg a day, which is well above what most capsules on a shelf provide. That is the specific reason I keep Nootropics Depot's 8:1 dual extract at 8.4 with a 9.2 on value: an 8:1 extract gets you into trial territory at a realistic capsule count.

Citicoline continues to be the ingredient with the cleanest human record. A 28-day randomised trial published in Food and Nutrition Sciences showed improved attention, an earlier study showed gains in attention and processing speed alongside MRI evidence of increased frontal lobe energy activity, and the safety record holds across trials up to 12 weeks. Effects typically show within one to two weeks. That combination of speed, evidence, and a cost of pennies per day is why Jarrow Citicoline 250 mg sits third at 9.0 with a 9.6 on evidence and a 9.8 on value. If you want to know whether this category does anything for you, start there for a month.

Mind Lab Pro v4 holds first at 9.3 because it delivers both citicoline and lion's mane at disclosed doses in one capsule, with two company-run clinical studies behind it and more in progress. Performance Lab Mind stays second at 9.0 for the same transparency at a lower cost per day. No rank or score changes today.

highlights.title: The lion's mane trial dose is 2,250 mg a day
highlights.body: The 2009 randomised controlled trial that produced significant cognitive gains in mild cognitive impairment used 750 mg three times daily. Check the label against that figure before assuming a single daily capsule replicates the study. An 8:1 dual extract is the practical way to reach a meaningful dose without swallowing a handful.

highlights.title: Citicoline is the fastest way to test whether this category works for you
highlights.body: A 28-day randomised trial in Food and Nutrition Sciences showed improved attention, and effects generally appear within one to two weeks. At 9.6 on evidence and 9.8 on value, Jarrow Citicoline 250 mg is the cheapest honest experiment available in this space, and one month is long enough to get an answer.

highlights.title: Disclosed doses are what separate the top of this board
highlights.body: Mind Lab Pro v4 scores 9.8 on transparency and Performance Lab Mind 9.6 because every ingredient amount is printed. When a label groups actives into a proprietary blend, you lose the ability to compare it against the trials, which is the whole basis for choosing one of these over another.

highlights.title: Twelve weeks is the length of the safety record, so plan reviews
highlights.body: Citicoline's clinical safety data runs to trials of up to 12 weeks. Treat that as a natural checkpoint: run a supplement for a defined period, note what changed in your actual work, then decide. Open-ended daily use without review is how people spend years on something they cannot evaluate.

en.commentary:
I hold this category to a stricter standard than most because the claims are large and the evidence is usually thin. My ranking rewards two things above all: ingredients with human trial support at the dose actually provided, and full label transparency rather than a proprietary blend.

Mind Lab Pro v4 holds first at 9.3 because it discloses every dose on the label and the formula is built from ingredients with the strongest evidence base, including citicoline, bacopa monnieri and lion's mane. When a company tells you exactly how much of each compound you are taking, you can compare that against the trial literature yourself. A proprietary blend prevents exactly that check, which is why I mark it down wherever it appears.

Jarrow Citicoline at 9.1 sits high for a reason that runs against how this category markets itself. It is a single ingredient at a clinically studied dose for a few dollars a month. Citicoline has the most consistent human data of any compound here, and buying it alone gives you the strongest evidence per dollar available.

Performance Lab Mind at 9.0 is the cleaner stimulant-free option.

One piece of advice worth more than any product on this list. Sleep, exercise and caffeine timing produce larger cognitive effects than every supplement here combined, and they are free. If those three are not sorted, a nootropic stack is treating a symptom.

highlights.title: Full dose disclosure is the first thing I check
highlights.body: A proprietary blend prevents you from comparing what you are taking against the trial literature, and that comparison is the only way to evaluate whether a formula is doing anything. Mind Lab Pro v4 discloses every dose, which is why it holds 9.3. Any product hiding behind a blend gets marked down regardless of what its ingredient list suggests.

highlights.title: Jarrow Citicoline is the best evidence per dollar in the category
highlights.body: A single ingredient at a clinically studied dose for a few dollars a month. Citicoline carries the most consistent human data of any compound on this list, and buying it on its own avoids paying for eleven other ingredients at doses below anything tested. At 9.1 it outranks products costing five times as much.

highlights.title: Fix sleep, exercise and caffeine timing first
highlights.body: These three produce larger cognitive effects than every supplement on this page combined, and all three are free. A stack layered on top of five hours of sleep is treating a symptom. Get those sorted for a month, and then evaluate whether a nootropic adds anything you can actually detect on top of that baseline.

highlights.title: Match the dose on the label to the dose in the study
highlights.body: Many formulas include an ingredient with genuine trial support at a fraction of the dose that was tested. Bacopa trials typically run at 300 milligrams of a standardised extract daily for twelve weeks. A product containing 50 milligrams is citing research it does not replicate, and reading that number is the check that separates real formulas from decorative ones.

zh-tw.commentary:

Mind Lab Pro v4 守第一，9.3 分，因為它把每一項的劑量都標在標籤上，配方也是用證據基礎最強的成分組成，包括胞磷膽鹼、假馬齒莧與獅鬃菇。當一家公司告訴你每一種化合物你吃進去多少，你就可以自己拿去對照試驗文獻。專利複方擋掉的正是這個查核，所以我看到就扣分。

Jarrow Citicoline 9.1 分排得高，理由跟這個品類的行銷方式剛好相反。它是單一成分、臨床研究劑量、一個月幾美元。胞磷膽鹼是這裡人體資料最一致的化合物，單買它就是每一塊錢買到最強證據的做法。

Performance Lab Mind 9.0 分，是比較乾淨的無刺激選項。

最後這個建議的價值大過榜單上任何產品。睡眠、運動與咖啡因的時間安排，帶來的認知效果大過這頁所有補充品加起來，而且不用錢。這三件事沒處理好，吃補腦品就是在治標。

highlights.title: 我第一個看的是有沒有完整標示劑量
highlights.body: 專利複方讓你無法把吃進去的東西拿去對照試驗文獻，而那個對照是評估配方有沒有作用的唯一方法。Mind Lab Pro v4 每一項劑量都標，所以拿 9.3。躲在複方後面的產品，不管成分表看起來多漂亮都要扣分。

highlights.title: 每一塊錢買到最多證據的是 Jarrow Citicoline
highlights.body: 單一成分、臨床研究劑量、一個月幾美元。胞磷膽鹼是這份榜單上人體資料最一致的化合物，單買它就避免了為另外十一種低於試驗劑量的成分付錢。9.1 分，勝過價格五倍的產品。

highlights.title: 先把睡眠、運動與咖啡因時間處理好
highlights.body: 這三件事帶來的認知效果大過這一頁所有補充品加起來，而且全部免費。在每天睡五小時的基礎上疊補腦配方，是在治標。先把這三件事做好一個月，再來評估補腦品在那個基準之上還加了什麼你真的感覺得到的東西。

highlights.title: 把標籤劑量對照研究劑量
highlights.body: 很多配方放的成分確實有試驗支持，劑量卻只有受試劑量的零頭。假馬齒莧的試驗通常是每天 300 毫克標準化萃取、持續十二週。一個只放 50 毫克的產品，引用的是它沒有複製的研究，而讀懂這個數字就是分辨真配方與裝飾配方的那道檢查。

en.commentary:
Mind Lab Pro v4 stays first at 9.3 and the 9.8 transparency score carries most of that. Every ingredient is disclosed at its dose, which sounds like a low bar until you read the labels in this category and count how many hide behind a proprietary blend. Two company backed clinical studies on the finished formula is more than almost anything here can claim, and the stack itself is sensible: 250 mg citicoline and 500 mg organic lion's mane doing the structural work.

That combination matches where the evidence actually sits. A 2015 trial found citicoline improved attention and processing speed with MRI showing raised frontal lobe energy activity, and it is one of the few ingredients here with a mechanism you can point at. Lion's mane now has three human trials, the strongest being a randomised controlled trial in adults with mild cognitive impairment that showed significant improvement at 750 mg taken three times daily. Note the dose. Most consumer products are well under it, which is the single most useful thing to check before buying.

Jarrow Citicoline 250 mg at 9.1 is the pick I recommend most often. It gives you the best evidenced single ingredient in the category at a 9.6 value score, and starting with one compound tells you whether it does anything for you before you spend on a nine ingredient stack.

On expectations, both citicoline and lion's mane build gradually over weeks of consistent daily use. Judge them at four weeks and beyond. Safety profiles in trials running up to twelve weeks are strong for citicoline, L-theanine and bacopa, which is the group I would build any stack around.

highlights.title: Full dose disclosure is the top score
highlights.body: Mind Lab Pro discloses every ingredient at its dose and carries two clinical studies on the finished formula. Its 9.8 transparency rating reflects a bar most of this category does not clear.

highlights.title: Citicoline has the clearest mechanism
highlights.body: A 2015 trial showed improved attention and processing speed with MRI evidence of raised frontal lobe energy activity. That is a specific, checkable result rather than a general claim.

highlights.title: Check the lion's mane dose before buying
highlights.body: The strongest trial used 750 mg three times daily in adults with mild cognitive impairment. Comparing a product's dose against that figure is the most useful minute you can spend.

highlights.title: Start with one ingredient
highlights.body: Jarrow Citicoline at a 9.6 value score gives you the best evidenced compound on its own. If it works for you, you learn that cheaply before buying a nine ingredient stack.

highlights.title: Judge results at four weeks
highlights.body: Citicoline and lion's mane both build gradually with consistent daily use. Trials up to twelve weeks show strong safety profiles for citicoline, L-theanine and bacopa.
